sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong Q2 with revenue of $3.1B (up 13% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 34% (up from 32.5% last year). However, forward guidance for Q3 revenue ($4.02B-$4.1B, 8-10% growth) implies a deceleration from Q2's 13% growth, and management explicitly warns of tougher year-over-year comparisons in Q4 that will 'put pressure on growth rates later in the year.' The full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of at least 34.5% is reaffirmed, not raised. The net effect is a modestly positive quarter with cautious forward language, warranting a score just above neutral.

summary.margin: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 34% in Q2 2025, up from 32.5% in Q2 2024. Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be at least 34.5%.
key_risks: Tougher year-over-year comparisons in Q4 2025 putting pressure on growth rates.
Year-over-year decline in adjusted EBITDA margin expected in Q3 and Q4 2025 due to growth investments and tougher top-line comparisons.
Approximately $200 million investment towards new businesses in 2025 with no meaningful near-term revenue expected.
key_opportunities: Acceleration in nights booked from April to July, with momentum globally and especially strong growth in the US.
Expansion markets (Latin America, Asia Pacific) growing at twice the rate of core markets for six consecutive quarters.
Launch of Airbnb Services and reimagined Airbnb Experiences, with over 60,000 applications to host and average guest rating of 4.93 stars.
New partnerships with Tour de France, Lollapalooza, IOC, and FIFA World Cup to build brand awareness and supply.
AI customer service agent reducing need for human agent contact by 15%.
New $6 billion share repurchase program announced.

net income of $642 million and EPS of $1.03 grew 16% and 20%, respectively.

evidence.claim: Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be at least 34.5%.

evidence.claim: Year-over-year decline in adjusted EBITDA margin expected in Q3 and Q4 2025 due to growth investments.

evidence.quote: This includes approximately $200 million of investment towards new businesses in 2025. While we don't expect meaningful revenue from our new businesses in the near term, we believe the opportunity is significant and are building with a multiyear view.

evidence.quote: As we look to Q3, we're encouraged by current demand trends, specifically the acceleration of nights booked from April through July. We've seen this momentum globally with especially strong growth in the US.

evidence.claim: Expansion markets growing at twice the rate of core markets for six consecutive quarters.
evidence.quote: Nights booked on an origin basis in our expansion markets have now grown at twice the rate of our core markets for six consecutive quarters.

evidence.quote: Since launch, over 60,000 people have submitted applications to host a service or experience. ... The average guest rating for a service and experience since launch is 4.93 stars out of 5 stars.

evidence.claim: New partnerships with Tour de France, Lollapalooza, IOC, and FIFA World Cup.

evidence.claim: AI customer service agent reducing need for human agent contact by 15%.
evidence.quote: We also expanded our new AI customer service agent in the US, reducing the percentage of hosting guests who needed to contact a human agent by 15%.

evidence.claim: New $6 billion share repurchase program announced.
evidence.quote: And today, we're announcing a new share repurchase program with authorization to purchase up to an additional $6 billion of our Class A common stock.

Airbnb had a strong Q2. We exceeded expectations across key metrics, including bookings, revenue and margins. ... As we look to Q3, we're encouraged by current demand trends, specifically the acceleration of nights booked from April through July.
